html:
GitHub

Enable the optional GitHub skill in capability selection, then create a GitHub Account in the Parameter Store editor. Prefer a fine-grained PAT restricted to the exact repositories and permissions needed. Enter its GitHub login, numeric account ID, token, explicit authorized_repositories (owner/repo names), and granted_permissions. The grant metadata is operator-declared; GitHub decides actual authorization. github.connection_status verifies the token's live login and ID. Tokens remain private in Parameter Store, including when ordinary redaction is off. Tool arguments contain account_ref, never the token.

The numeric account ID is the id returned by GitHub's public https://api.github.com/users/LOGIN endpoint for that login; use the user ID, not an organization or repository ID. Keep profile credentials in the Parameter Store editor.

This implementation supports github.com user PATs. Classic PATs are explicitly marked as legacy/broader credentials and require credential_type=classic_pat; no token type is guessed from its prefix. OAuth, GitHub Apps and Enterprise hosts are not implemented. There is no automatic token upgrade or repository allowlist expansion.

Git Working Context and Shell continue to own working trees, local branches, commits, status, diffs, checkout, rebase, fetch, pull and push. Compose “commit and open a PR” by committing and pushing through Shell, then calling GitHub. Provider tools never run local Git commands.

Discovery and exact targets

The five entry tools are github.accounts, github.connection_status, github.repo, github.issues and github.pull_request. Discover github through the existing catalog, then its returned sections. Enabling the skill does not authorize a provider mutation.

Section (prefix github.) Tool suffixes (prefix github.)
connection accounts, connection_status
repositories repo, branches, tags, commits, commit, compare, contents
issues.read issues, issue, issue_comments
issues.write issue_create, issue_update, issue_comment, issue_close, issue_reopen
pulls.read pull_requests, pull_request, pull_files, pull_commits, pull_reviews, pull_comments, pull_checks
pulls.write pull_create, pull_update, pull_comment, pull_request_reviewers, pull_review, pull_merge
actions.read workflow_runs, workflow_run, workflow_jobs, workflow_logs, workflow_artifacts, workflow_artifact_download, checks
actions.write workflow_dispatch, workflow_run_cancel, workflow_run_rerun
releases.read releases, release, release_assets
releases.write release_create, release_update, release_publish, release_delete, release_asset_upload, release_asset_delete
notifications notifications, notification_thread

Reads resolve explicit owner/repo first, then repository_ref or an accepted git_repository parameter, then complete, verified Git Working Context remotes. Only literal github.com HTTPS and Git SSH URLs are recognized. SSH aliases, credentials in URLs and unrelated hosts are rejected. Multiple distinct GitHub repositories, including fork plus upstream, are ambiguous; neither origin nor the first remote is privileged. Explicit account references take precedence over accepted accounts; otherwise exactly one configured account must exist.

First call github.repo and inspect the returned identity. Every write requires explicit account_ref, account_id, host, owner, repo, and repository_id from that read, plus the exact object ID/number and desired change. This binds the existing confirmation to a concrete principal and repository. The live account and repository IDs are verified before the mutation; profile revisions are checked again at every authenticated request.

Permissions

Checked against official GitHub documentation on 2026-10-01. Permission names below use GitHub's API keys; statuses is the UI's Commit statuses. Write includes read. Metadata read is required for the repository preflight and is automatically included with fine-grained repository access. Public endpoints may work with fewer permissions, but this adapter uses the documented private-resource contract for predictable behavior.

Tools (prefix github.) Fine-grained permission requirements
accounts Local metadata; no API permission
connection_status Authenticated /user; no additional permission
repo metadata:read
branches, tags, commits, commit, compare, contents contents:read
issues, issue issues:read
issue_comments issues:read OR pull_requests:read
issue_create issues:write
issue_update, issue_close, issue_reopen, issue_comment, pull_comment issues:write OR pull_requests:write
pull_requests, pull_request, pull_files, pull_commits, pull_reviews, pull_comments pull_requests:read
pull_create, pull_update, pull_request_reviewers, pull_review pull_requests:write
pull_merge contents:write; pull_requests:read for the head preflight
checks checks:read AND statuses:read
pull_checks pull_requests:read AND checks:read AND statuses:read
workflow_runs, workflow_run, workflow_jobs, workflow_logs, workflow_artifacts, workflow_artifact_download actions:read
workflow_dispatch, workflow_run_cancel, workflow_run_rerun actions:write
releases, release, release_assets contents:read
release_create, release_update, release_publish, release_delete, release_asset_upload, release_asset_delete contents:write
notifications, notification_thread Fine-grained PAT unsupported; explicit classic PAT with notifications or repo scope

Release creation checks an existing tag; it does not create tags or modify workflow files. GitHub documents additional Workflows permission in some release/tag creation situations; the adapter surfaces accepted permission diagnostics if GitHub requires it instead of silently broadening authority. Notifications for private resources can require classic repo scope and organization/SSO approval. A fine-grained account is never silently replaced.

github.permission_missing identifies the feature and required or provider-accepted permission sets. Within a set all permissions are required; alternatives mean any one complete set. Correct the selected token's permissions/repository selection and organization approval, then update its declared grants. A 404 can mean inaccessible private data; it does not prove absence.

Provider behavior and bounds

Requests use X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2026-03-10, Accept: application/vnd.github+json, a User-Agent and private Bearer authorization. Raw contents use the documented raw media type. No preview media types, arbitrary REST URLs or GraphQL input are exposed.

Lists fetch one page, default 25 and maximum 100 objects. Supply next_page explicitly with the same filters; pages are capped at 1000. Link URLs are never executed. GitHub's own endpoint caps still apply, including PR file/commit limits. compare returns the paginated commits; use pull_files for PR changed files. JSON transport is capped at 2 MiB; projections have a 48K-character/1500-node budget, 8000 characters per string, 100 elements per nested list and explicit truncation. contents supports bounded directory listings and small UTF-8 files; large/binary reads use as_artifact=true. Directory reads do not recursively crawl.

Requests use connect/read timeouts of 10/45 seconds, a 60-second socket deadline and a 180-second invocation deadline. Task cancellation aborts owned sockets. Reads retry a transport failure or server error once, after a cancellable one-second delay. Throttling returns safe remaining/reset/resource/request-ID diagnostics and retains Retry-After/reset backoff across invocations in bounded process memory. Secondary limits without an explicit delay defer for at least 60 seconds. There is no sleeping retry of throttled writes and no generic mutation retry. Process restart clears the in-memory backoff, so callers must also respect the returned delay. Conditional GET/304 handling exists in the client; there is no persistent provider cache.

issues filters PRs out of the provider's mixed issue pages. Labels and assignees in issue_update are desired-state sets. pull_requests(head="owner:branch") locates a branch's PR. General PR comments use pull_comment/issue_comments; pull_comments reads inline review comments. pull_review requires explicit COMMENT, APPROVE or REQUEST_CHANGES and an exact commit ID. pull_merge requires a reviewed expected_head_sha and explicit merge method; that SHA is also sent as GitHub's merge precondition. Inspect checks first; repository branch protections remain authoritative and are never bypassed.

Workflow dispatch requires an exact workflow ID/filename, ref and bounded dictionary with at most 25 inputs. GitHub validates workflow-declared input names/types; no model infers them. The current API's workflow_run_id is retained as accepted-run evidence. Run status and conclusion come directly from GitHub; no percentage is invented.

Release creation is draft-first and requires an existing tag. Publication uses an inspected exact draft release ID. Upload accepts conversation-owned artifact://, art_ or artifact-workspace:// sources, verifies the immutable size/hash, then streams bytes once. Gateway files must enter the existing Artifact/File transfer path first. Downloads become sensitive conversation artifacts, capped at 100 MiB; ZIPs remain unextracted. Signed download redirects receive no API headers, cookies or token. Interrupted downloads publish no partial artifact. Release asset deletion is explicit, never automatic collision repair.

Uncertain outcomes and confirmation

All 20 writes use the existing confirmation architecture. Merge, dispatch, cancel/rerun, release publication/upload and release/asset deletion also use the native unsafe-action policy. Every successful provider mutation receipt includes exact account/repository identity.

Mutation family Lost-response behavior and reconciliation
Issue/PR creation, comments, reviews, reviewer requests Outcome unknown; never repeat or deduplicate by text. Inspect provider identifiers independently.
Issue close/reopen Read exact issue; matching desired state is reconciliation evidence, with attribution explicitly unproven.
Issue/PR update Outcome unknown; read and compare the exact object before deciding on new work.
Merge Read exact PR; only merged=true with the same expected head permits desired-state reconciliation. No second merge.
Workflow dispatch Specialized unknown error; inspect runs at exact workflow/ref. Never dispatch twice after response loss.
Run cancel/rerun Outcome unknown; inspect exact run status and attempt. No automatic repeat.
Release creation/update/deletion, asset deletion Outcome unknown; inspect exact provider identity/state. No generic replay.
Release publish Read exact release; draft=false supplies desired-state evidence. Otherwise specialized unknown error.
Asset upload Specialized unknown error. Inspect asset ID, name, size and digest; name/size alone do not prove attribution. Never upload twice automatically.

Transport loss, server errors, malformed/oversized success responses and cancellation after write dispatch produce uncertain-effect receipts. The existing runtime replay guard blocks automatic repeat attempts. Explicit provider validation/auth/rate rejection remains a known rejection. These distinctions do not depend on error copy or helper inference.

All provider content is untrusted_external_data, including issue instructions, workflow logs, errors and filenames. Provider text cannot choose tools, change grants or access private tokens. The main Agent handles interpretation. The shared content policy excludes provider bodies from diagnostics; canonical redaction removes credential reflections from tool output. There are zero helper/classifier/model calls in this skill.

Organization administration, billing, repository deletion/transfer, secrets, deploy keys, rulesets, webhooks, package deletion, Codespaces, Copilot administration, app installation administration and arbitrary GraphQL are outside this skill.
